# HR Laws & Compliance Requirements

| Jurisdiction | Requirement relevant to HR operations |
| --- | --- |
| Mainland China | PIPL requires a lawful basis and appropriate protection for employee information. HR processing under labour rules or collective agreements must still follow necessity, transparency and security duties. |
| Mainland China | Significant automated HR decisions require fairness, explanation and a human review or appeal path. AI screening should assist rather than silently determine hiring outcomes. |
| Mainland China | The 2024 cross-border data rules provide a conditional HR-management route for certain employee transfers, but do not remove other PIPL obligations. |
| Mainland China | Face-recognition rules effective 1 June 2025 emphasise necessity and minimisation; non-biometric attendance options should remain available where they can achieve the same purpose. |
| Mainland China | Personal-information compliance audits effective 1 May 2025 make data maps, access history and audit exports valuable for larger processors. Labour, social-insurance, tax, wage and working-time rules require regional and effective-date versioning. |
| European Union | GDPR and the EU AI Act treat employment and recruitment AI as a high-governance area; maintain data governance, logs, technical documentation and human oversight ahead of the relevant 2027 high-risk obligations. |
| United States | Federal rules are supplemented by anti-discrimination enforcement and local requirements such as New York City’s automated employment decision-tool rules. |
| Singapore and ASEAN | PDPA and regional responsible-AI guidance support privacy, accountability and explainability; country-specific employment and data requirements still apply. |
